rows.purpose: Open or resume a full-model session with its exact saved state, work context and recoverable history.
rows.reason: F-SESSION requires interruption-safe resume, while charter section 4 replaces the 0.4 runtime and process split with a new application. Rebuild startup around verified model loading and session recovery rather than inheriting the server launch interface.
requirements: X-01: Preserve the exact hashed asset and source-bound proof bytes across checkouts and installations; exercise line-ending conversion without weakening manifest verification or changing model identity.
Validate model identity, checkpoint hashes and chronological journal replay before publishing readiness; refuse concurrent ownership of the same session and preserve current work on recovery failure.

Resume the shared context and preferences through the session store; keep platform startup and file access outside the mathematical engine, with EngineProcess ownership if a local engine child is used.

rows.purpose: Understand supported launch options and their effects before opening or changing a session.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PLATFORM need understandable entry and diagnostics, but charter section 4 does not preserve the 0.4 server executable or its flags. Re-host launch help with the selected 1.0 entry and supported options.
requirements: Help must work before model loading or session acquisition, have no session side effects and describe only supported 1.0 options in English.

rows.purpose: Leave the application with durable work saved and application-owned resources released.
rows.reason: F-SESSION requires safe interruption and charter section 4 replaces the old listener and process arrangement. Preserve graceful shutdown guarantees in the new lifecycle boundary.
requirements: Stop admission, cancel unfinished analysis, persist timer and workspace bookkeeping and release the session lock in order, without undoing a durable commit.
If a local engine child is used, stop only the matching owned launch through EngineProcess; stalled or trickling clients must not defeat bounded graceful shutdown.

rows.purpose: Recover session ownership and release resources when the application that owns an engine disappears.
rows.reason: F-SESSION interruption safety and AGENTS.md process ownership remain binding; charter section 4 leaves the 1.0 process arrangement new. Retain parent-death recovery wherever an owned child is used without requiring the 0.4 process split.
requirements: Use EngineProcess parent-pipe recovery for an owned local engine child; owner disappearance must preserve committed state and eventually release the session lock.
Parent-death handling must stop bookkeeping and resources without executing a solving operation or terminating an unrelated process.

rows.purpose: Enter the workspace and resume the selected solving or exploration context.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-LEARN retain the entry purpose; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 7 requires one workspace and path for everyone. Charter section 4 replaces the separate 0.4 browser entry with the new shell.
requirements: Provide one entry with direct context resume and an explicitly labelled full-model practice copy, with optional coaching tied to the chosen task.
Opening the workspace must not execute a puzzle operation or create a second route around the command layer.

rows.purpose: Know that the application's engine is ready and belongs to the intended session and model.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM requires trustworthy readiness before F-SESSION publishes usable state. Charter section 4 changes the runtime boundary, so retain readiness and identity checks without freezing the 0.4 HTTP response or interpreter fields.
requirements: Report readiness only after complete model verification and session recovery; bind it to the current model, session and owned launch where applicable.
Use authenticated EngineProcess health checks for a local engine child; readiness must not depend on public network access or expose credentials.

rows.purpose: Load the separate browser client executable scripts and styles.
rows.reason: Charter section 4 replaces the 0.4 runtime and separate client arrangement. No provisional flow requires the old browser script bundle or its HTTP whitelist.
rows.notes: Proposal requiring owner signature; this row covers delivery of the 0.4 browser bundle, while entry to the solving workspace is retained by U1-005. The U3-002 link applies to its browser-asset delivery portion.

rows.purpose: Obtain verified full-model geometry and sticker identifiers for drawing and inspection.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE need real geometry and exact correspondence to the puzzle; charter sections 2 and 4 retain the immutable model while changing the renderer and transport. Move asset delivery to the new renderer boundary.
requirements: Validate immutable manifest identity and asset digests before exposing geometry; preserve all 259,800 sticker slots and their canonical identifiers.
Deliver immutable geometry through the platform boundary without requiring browser HTTP assets or granting the renderer authority to relabel mechanical state.

rows.purpose: Stop an unfinished analysis and learn its authoritative outcome without losing committed work.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-SESSION need cancellable work, and the command table separates command outcome from display refresh. Rebuild cancellation as a job lifecycle operation rather than a shared unqualified flag.
requirements: Bind cancellation to the active job and acknowledge its terminal outcome; cancellation before publication leaves state and recovery data unchanged.
A cancellation request after durable commit must return the committed receipt and never imply that the action was rolled back; retain the solver draft when cancelling analysis.

rows.purpose: Observe an analysis job's progress, result or typed failure while continuing to use the workspace.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-SESSION require responsive job observation; the command table requires cancellable jobs and separate durable outcomes. Replace HTTP polling details with the new command and view-model lifecycle.
requirements: Expose stable job identity, running and terminal states, typed errors and cancellation status without synchronous waits on the UI thread.
Keep durable command receipts distinct from analysis errors and stale display; a retry must not create a second commit.

rows.purpose: Read a coherent account of the current state, residuals, protection, work context and available recovery actions.
rows.reason: F-SESSION, F-TARGET and F-ENDGAME rely on exact residual state; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 requires Global and Local to share context and revision. Replace the monolithic status response with coherent revision-bound view data.
requirements: B-005: Capture a coherent immutable status under short read synchronization, then release session ownership before serialization or delivery; verify that a stalled consumer cannot block session work.

X-02: Keep checkpoint metadata access lightweight and independent of compressed label blobs; status and command receipts must avoid checkpoint-history scans, with measurements over growing checkpoint populations.
Expose state, workspace and protection revisions plus the full-state hash; distinguish exact completion, permitted residuals, unknown frames, execution permission and learning attainment.
Build both linked views from the same authoritative snapshot, with explicit stale and busy states and without another mutable copy of puzzle state.

rows.purpose: Inspect canonical cell and vertex structure, incidence, adjacency and exact model geometry.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and F-LEARN require the real polytope structure, and charter section 2 freezes geometry and identifiers. Re-host the same structural mathematics and results behind the engine boundary.
requirements: Preserve canonical numbering, fixed centers, piece-layer definitions and actual four-dimensional geometry; adjacency routes are navigation rather than legal turn sequences.
Structure queries and rendering filters must leave all mechanical labels and generators unchanged.

rows.purpose: Read the exact orbit definitions, orientation information and published seed witnesses with their collateral.
rows.reason: F-TARGET, F-MACRO and F-ENDGAME use the orbit and raw-seed mathematics recorded in solving-workflow sections 2 and 3. Preserve the catalogue as mathematical reference under charter section 2 and the section 7 human-solve boundary.
requirements: B-005: Capture catalogue data without retaining the session lock during serialization or delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Retain every orbit, immutable seed identity, finite legal witness and full collateral; never infer stage order from orbit IDs or discard non-target effects.
Catalogue lookup must not choose or synthesize a solving macro from current state; use in an operation requires the solver's explicit entry or selection and fresh complete-effect review.

rows.purpose: Browse recorded operations and their journal branches, witnesses, provenance and exact state identities.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-EXECUTE need persistent inspectable history, as solving-workflow section 4.2 requires consistent recovery and undo. Preserve chronological event and branch semantics while re-hosting the history query.
requirements: B-005: Copy a bounded history page under read synchronization and release it before serialization or delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Preserve parent links, cursors, chronological replay evidence, pre/post hashes and recorded assistance provenance; provenance must not confer execution permission or human-solve certification.

rows.purpose: Return to a selected recorded journal branch with exact verified state and current preferences preserved.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-EXECUTE require recoverable branch navigation; solving-workflow section 4.2 retains current global protection on return. Preserve checkpoint-assisted chronological replay and branch retention.
requirements: B-004: Admit checkout jobs atomically with other long operations; an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture must prove that at most one active job owns the session.
Verify every replay hash before publishing the selected head, retain all other branches and current preferences and protection, and invalidate preview and execution authority.
Cancellation or failure before publication must leave the previous head recoverable, and completion must be reported separately from display refresh.

rows.purpose: Understand recorded work and elapsed solving effort without confusing counts or time with correctness.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-LEARN retain reports; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design sections 1 and 5 distinguish progress, learning, permission and completion and require local measurements. Consolidate journal statistics and attempt metrics into the authoritative report.
requirements: B-005: Capture report inputs and release session synchronization before serialization or delivery; verify that a slow report consumer cannot block commands.
Keep scramble and solver work, primitive and star counts, transactions, imported provenance, timer and competence measurements distinct; time alone must not certify a solve or a skill.
Keep metrics local and optional where collection is user-facing; timer persistence belongs to the session store rather than the mathematical engine or an implicit report write.

rows.purpose: Undo the last complete recorded operation and recover its exact prior labelled state.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and charter section 5 E4 require available undo without losing work. Preserve whole-transaction inversion, pre-state hash verification and branch retention.
requirements: X-02: Undo receipts must avoid checkpoint-blob scans and unbounded status rebuilding; verify response work over growing checkpoint populations.
Invert the complete chronological legal witness, verify its pre-state hash and durably move the journal head while preserving the redo choice and other branches.
Invalidate old preview authority and report the durable undo separately from refresh; withdrawing a current achievement must retain already unlocked explanations and saved macros.

rows.purpose: Redo an explicitly chosen recorded operation on its matching journal branch.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and solving-workflow section 4.2 require exact undo/redo continuity. Preserve ancestry and full-state checks, with an explicit branch choice when redo is ambiguous.
requirements: X-02: Redo receipts must avoid checkpoint-blob scans and unbounded status rebuilding; verify response work over growing checkpoint populations.
Require the matching parent and pre-state, replay the same complete legal witness and verify the post-state before publication; never choose an ambiguous redo branch automatically.
Invalidate old preview authority and preserve current global protection policy and durable outcome reporting.

rows.purpose: Inspect every legal cap rotation and its inverse word, axis, order and four-dimensional rotation data.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE require legal Grip and Twist input; solving-workflow section 4.3 preserves access to all 1,200 generators. Re-host the same cap-rotation mathematics without inheriting old controls.
requirements: B-005: Release session synchronization before serializing or delivering grip records; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Preserve all eleven nonidentity rotations per cap, legal finite words, inverse relationships and exact four-dimensional axes; no camera or display filter may alter their meaning or reachability.

rows.purpose: Save a named exact state and journal position for later verified recovery.
rows.reason: F-PROTECT and F-SESSION need checkpoints under solving-workflow section 4.2. Preserve labelled snapshots, hashes, head identity and the protected solved-root checkpoint.
requirements: Store the complete label array, matching full-state hash, journal head and saved preferences atomically; a saved-root checkpoint must not be overwritten by an unsolved head.
Expose replacement of an existing named checkpoint as an explicit action and retain journal recovery; checkpoint metadata must remain separable from compressed label blobs.

rows.purpose: Know which complete physical pieces and sticker slots belong to a specified cap.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE rely on exact affecting-cap membership, and charter section 2 freezes this mathematics. Preserve the complete piece-closed mask independently of visibility.
requirements: B-005: Capture or obtain the immutable cap mask and release session synchronization before delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Return membership for all 259,800 sticker slots with whole-piece closure and canonical cell validation; distinguish hosting cells from the full set of affecting caps.

rows.purpose: Recover a verified checkpoint while keeping current work and protection decisions recoverable.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PROTECT retain checkpoint restoration, while solving-workflow section 4.2 forbids an old orbit context from rolling back current global protection. Redesign restoration scope instead of blindly reinstalling checkpoint preferences.
requirements: Validate the complete checkpoint, model and hash before one transactional state/head publication; retain the prior recoverable head and invalidate previews and execution authority.
Preserve current global protection on context resume; any intentional restoration of saved preferences or protection must have explicit scope and must not silently overwrite current decisions.
Expose the durable recovery outcome separately from a failed or stale display refresh.

rows.purpose: Resolve displayed sticker and turn identifiers to their verified canonical mechanical counterparts.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-EXECUTE require trustworthy picking and move identity under charter section 2. Charter section 4 replaces the retained host, so redesign correspondence for the canonical renderer boundary rather than retaining a native-map HTTP contract.
requirements: B-005: Deliver immutable correspondence data outside session synchronization; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Bind correspondence to the frozen model and current renderer identity, preserving every sticker and legal generator; canonical IDs may make a separate runtime remapping unnecessary.
Any retained MPUlt numbering conversion belongs to offline legacy-data compatibility or oracle evidence and must not require the old runtime in the 1.0 product.

rows.purpose: Return explicitly to the exact solved root while preserving preferences and a recovery point for prior progress.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-LEARN need a recoverable reset; AGENTS.md requires transactional reset with current preferences and a recovery checkpoint retained. Preserve this contract independently of the new shell.
requirements: Validate any supplied camera before writes, create the Before reset recovery checkpoint and select exact labelled identity in one transaction without deleting prior branches.
Retain current preferences and timer, invalidate pending execution authority and ensure cancellation or write failure leaves the prior session recoverable.
Reset must follow the solver's explicit action and must not blanket-lock a new solved state or silently reverse a manual protection decision.

rows.purpose: Receive one revision-consistent picture of mechanical state, appearance, interaction scope and progress.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-RELATE and F-CHECK require coherent views; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 binds Global and Local to one context and revision. Replace native transport arrays and delta protocol with the new view-model boundary while retaining atomicity.
requirements: B-005: Freeze a coherent snapshot under short read synchronization and release it before encoding or delivery; verify a consumer larger than transport buffers cannot hold session work.
X-02: Snapshot status must use lightweight checkpoint metadata and avoid label-blob scans; measure cost as checkpoint history grows.
Bind labels, presentation, interaction masks and summaries to state/workspace/protection revisions; delta bases must be immutable and unknown bases must yield a full snapshot.
Keep display references distinct from interactive objects, and tie any explicitly marked forecast comparison to the same authoritative pre-state without mutating mechanical state.

rows.purpose: Create a consistent durable backup of the entire session and its recoverable work.
rows.reason: F-SESSION needs complete recovery beyond a selected-branch export; charter section 4 gives the new session store ownership of persistence. The owner migration decision of 2 October requires a locked SQLite online backup for the legacy source without selecting a 1.0 storage format.
requirements: Include all journal branches, checkpoints, workspace and preferences in a consistent backup; validate its identity and publish it durably without changing the live session.
For a 0.4 migration source, copy under the session lock with the SQLite online backup API, never a file copy or immutable=1, and never modify the original directory.
Keep 1.0 backup-format selection separate from the legacy copy mechanism and the migration-format freeze.

rows.purpose: Draw the current puzzle appearance with explicit roles, status and exact identity correspondence.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK retain rendering data; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 2 requires one encoding grammar with class colour and separate identity, role and status channels. Replace native colour/style arrays as an independent presentation contract.
requirements: B-005: Freeze appearance data and release session synchronization before encoding or delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Bind appearance channels to the authoritative label and view revisions; colour carries class rather than identity, with exact IDs and fixed anchors resolving repeated colours.
Keep protection conflicts and complete-operation effects visible through filters; appearance and theme changes must neither relabel state nor silently alter picking eligibility.

rows.purpose: Read the exact current label of every mechanical sticker independently of what is visible.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-PLATFORM need complete state evidence; charter section 2 preserves all 259,800 labelled slots. Re-host the full ordered label-array contract.
requirements: B-005: Freeze the full label array under read synchronization and release it before delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Preserve canonical slot order and unsigned 32-bit label values, bind the array to model identity, revision and full-state hash, and never project it through display filters.

rows.purpose: Read recoverable elapsed solving time and whether the solver-controlled timer is running.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and the local measurements of owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 5 use elapsed time; solving-workflow section 4.2 retains consistent interruption recovery. Preserve explicit timer control and periodic persistence as bookkeeping.
requirements: Status and heartbeat must not start or pause the timer; include thinking time and persist the elapsed total through interruption without changing puzzle labels.
Keep timer clock and persistence outside the mathematical engine, local only, and distinguish elapsed time from correctness and exact completion.
rows.notes: The command table leaves timer storage and undo classification open; this row preserves the elapsed-time contract without deciding that classification.

rows.purpose: See filtered work, reference context and complete-operation effects without confusing visibility with permission.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-CHECK require the three scopes separated in solving-workflow section 4.3. Owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 2 replaces fixed style codes with the common encoding grammar and mandatory conflict visibility.
requirements: B-005: Freeze view-style results and release session synchronization before serialization or delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Separate full mechanical analysis, the work/interaction filter and noninteractive references; a displayed buffer or effect must not become pickable or twistable merely by being drawn.
Always expose protected damage and complete-operation collateral, including outside the focus or display set; no style or theme may alter mechanical labels.

rows.purpose: Explicitly begin elapsed solving-time accumulation without changing the puzzle.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-LEARN retain the explicit timer recorded in solving-workflow section 4.2 and the command table. Preserve idempotent start semantics rather than inferring a start from activity.
requirements: Starting an already running timer must be idempotent; persist the total and running state through the session store and include thinking time.
The timer must remain local and must not drive puzzle operations, automatic solving or completion certification.

rows.purpose: Export the complete legal witness and exact source-to-destination effect of a reviewed operation.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-REUSE need independently inspectable certificates, and charter section 2 preserves finite legal witnesses and full collateral. Re-host certificate retrieval and export for the solver's operation.
requirements: B-005: Freeze the certificate and expanded witness before releasing session synchronization, then serialize or deliver outside it; verify slow-consumer isolation.
Bind certificate identity, source/destination arrays, chronological finite legal word and complete collateral to the immutable model and reviewed pre/post hashes.
Exporting a certificate must not select a solving macro or execute it; distinguish source/headless verification from actual Windows/DirectX evidence.

rows.purpose: Explicitly pause solving-time accumulation while preserving the elapsed total.
rows.reason: F-SESSION interruption and the command table retain explicit timer pause. Preserve the idempotent elapsed-time contract, including preservation through reset and recovery.
requirements: Pause must add the current interval once and durably preserve the total; pausing an already paused timer must not change it.
Keep clock and persistence outside the mathematical engine and timer values separate from progress or legal execution permission.

rows.purpose: Export a verifiable record of the selected session history and exact state for later recovery.
rows.reason: F-SESSION retains portable records, while charter section 4 assigns exports to the new session store and command layer. Owner-decisions-2026-10-02-migration requires a new history boundary at migration, so the old identity-root export cannot define every 1.0 archive.
requirements: B-005: Capture an immutable branch export and release session synchronization before encoding or file delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.

Preserve chronological legal witnesses, source identity, pre/post/final hashes, counts and provenance; enforce matching export/import budgets or offer a complete backup before producing an unusable record.

Use the frozen 1.0 archive format and migration checkpoint boundary, retaining legacy history as archive evidence; selected-branch export must disclose that other branches and checkpoints require a complete backup.

rows.purpose: Keep work context, preferences, macros, sets and protection decisions durable and consistent.
rows.reason: F-SESSION, F-PROTECT and F-REUSE retain persistent work; charter section 4 separates session store, commands and view model. Replace the broad preference payload with typed revision-aware workspace and protection changes.
requirements: Validate all supplied fields before an atomic write and publish related orbit, workspace and caller context changes together; failure must retain the previous consistent context.
Track workspace and protection revisions and invalidate review on changes to its actual inputs; retain position, identity and block protection as well as orbit protection.
Do not restore old global protection with an orbit context or silently relabel pieces, change key meanings or execute a macro through a preference update.

rows.purpose: Obtain a portable proof log of the recorded solve with exact replay evidence and provenance.
rows.reason: F-SESSION retains proof-log export; charter section 4 unifies file-changing actions under commands, and the owner migration decision of 2 October changes the history boundary. Consolidate proof export with the versioned 1.0 archive contract.
requirements: B-005: Freeze log data and release session synchronization before compression, serialization or delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.

Preserve full legal witnesses, chronological hashes, model identity, declared history scope and timer/provenance metadata; export must satisfy its matching importer budgets or explain a backup alternative.
Keep 0.4 proof decoding for one-way legacy import, with old history archived and 1.0 history rooted at the migration point; final format is subject to the migration-format freeze.

rows.purpose: Focus a canonical physical cell within the shared solving and inspection context.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE retain physical-cell focus; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 requires the two views to share context. Re-host focus as exact identity-based view context rather than a colour-driven host control.
requirements: Use canonical physical-cell identity and fixed geometry, with focus and its clear action shared across Global and Local at one revision.
Focus or hover must not silently assign a target, select a Grip, move the camera, change keys or grant execution permission; colour classes must not stand in for identity.

rows.purpose: Export the recorded solve as a portable interchange log with declared exactness and limits.
rows.reason: F-SESSION retains log interchange, but charter section 4 replaces the retained MPUlt runtime and the command table unifies exports. Consolidate the legacy-format purpose into the explicit log export contract with offline compatibility where provided.
requirements: B-005: Capture export inputs and release session synchronization before conversion, encoding or delivery; verify slow-consumer isolation.

Expose the chosen format, full-model identity, witness coverage, timer, checksum and resource limits; preserve exact labelled replay evidence in the native 1.0 archive even when an interchange format carries colours.

Any MPUlt v1 codec must be offline and use verified immutable numbering data without a live retained host; unsupported or over-budget export must leave the session intact and offer a verifiable archive or backup.
rows.notes: This preserves the user log-export purpose; the final supported output formats remain a format-freeze decision, not an authorization to inherit the 0.4 runtime.

rows.purpose: Select and follow the physical identity currently occupying an explicitly named position.
rows.reason: F-FIND requires following a piece separately from watching a fixed destination; solving-workflow section 4.3 separates inspection and role assignment. Re-host explicit selection in the shared view model and command context.
requirements: Resolve the occupant from the current authoritative revision and retain its immutable identity as pieces move; explicit ID selection may inspect a hidden piece without making it interactive.
Selection must not implicitly assign Target, Current, buffers or Grip, execute a turn or modify the mechanical label array.

rows.purpose: Select a physical piece from an eligible visible sticker hit and follow its identity.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-NAVIGATE preserve picking; solving-workflow section 4.3 separates interaction eligibility from noninteractive reference display. Replace retained-native hit mapping with the canonical renderer pick contract.
requirements: Bind hits to model identity and acknowledged state/view revisions, resolve the exact canonical sticker and occupant, and reject stale or ineligible hits.
Drawing a reference or effect outside the work filter must not make it pickable or twistable; selecting a hit must remain separate from role assignment and a live turn.

rows.purpose: Compare an inspected physical piece's current location and frame with its exact Home location and frame.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE retain Home/current inspection; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design sections 2 and 6 require fixed anchors and an intuitive shared relationship grammar. Replace host-specific home-centre annotation with exact comparison data.
requirements: Resolve the clicked identity at the current acknowledged revision and show Home versus current cells and frames with exact IDs and verified or unknown frame evidence.
Use real geometry and the glossary; do not substitute matching face colours for Home identity, and keep inspection separate from selecting a target, Grip or camera movement.

rows.purpose: Check the exact membership and visibility changes of a proposed Boolean work filter before applying it.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE requires explicit filters and separate work/reference scopes in solving-workflow section 4.3. Preserve Boolean predicate, ordered-rule and context-hash semantics as a read-only contract.
requirements: Evaluate valid expressions over the full model without changing labels or stored rules; preserve whole-piece membership, first-match rule order and exact matched/visible/added/removed counts.

Bind the preview context to every state, workspace and protection input used by its predicates; count work-filter results separately from added noninteractive references and mandatory effect overlays.

rows.purpose: Find the exact physical identity required at an inspected destination and compare its current frame with that destination.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-TARGET require relating the wanted piece to its destination; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 requires linked Local/Global comparison. Replace a native colour annotation and coupled buffer lookup with shared exact inspection.
requirements: Validate the acknowledged canonical destination and view revision, distinguish the destination from its occupant and wanted identity, and show exact current and required frames.

Inspection alone must not assign the target or generate an insertion macro; buffer/setup analysis requires the target named by the solver and reports fixed centers, buffers and unavailable references explicitly.

rows.purpose: Apply a reviewed work filter without hiding mechanical effects or silently widening interaction scope.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE retains stale-context validation; solving-workflow section 4.3 and owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 2 require noninteractive references and conflicts/effects to remain distinct. Replace the old blanket disabling of extra context with explicit scopes.
requirements: Revalidate the exact preview context and rules before atomic workspace publication; stale or invalid requests must retain the previous filter.
Apply only work/display eligibility, never mechanical state or full analysis; complete-operation collateral and protection conflicts must remain visible regardless of the applied filter.
Reference visibility and interaction eligibility must be separate, and filter changes must not silently rebind keys or roles.

rows.purpose: Clear an inspection annotation while retaining the chosen work context and cell focus.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-NAVIGATE need reversible inspection distinct from target, Grip and camera actions under solving-workflow section 4.3. Preserve annotation clearing as a view/workspace action with no puzzle effect.
requirements: Remove only the inspection annotation and its overlay, retaining focus, filters, selected roles and mechanical state; do not discard the solver draft or alter protection.

rows.purpose: Inspect a fixed position occupant, labels, orbit, cells and exact positional and orientation correctness.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-TARGET and F-ENDGAME need the exact occupant/position distinction described in solving-workflow section 3. Preserve the canonical position query and its mathematical results.
requirements: Return exact immutable occupant identity, current and Home relations, full sticker slots/labels and distinct position, orientation and labelled correctness at one state revision.
Unknown frame evidence must remain unknown, and a colour match or permitted residual must never be reported as exact completion.

rows.purpose: Locate a chosen physical piece identity's current position and exact piece state.
rows.reason: F-FIND requires piece-focused tracking while buffers and destinations remain positions, as solving-workflow sections 3.1 and 4 specify. Preserve exact identity-to-current-position lookup.
requirements: Validate immutable identity against the full model and resolve it at the current authoritative revision independently of visibility; return its exact current and Home information.
Tracking must not silently substitute the current occupant of an old position, reassign roles or execute a macro.

rows.purpose: Save a durable verifiable solve log with an explicit file identity for later recovery.
rows.reason: F-SESSION retains atomic proof-log saving, while charter section 4 routes all file changes through the command layer and owner migration path B changes the archive boundary. Consolidate save and export delivery around the 1.0 log contract.
requirements: Capture complete chronological witnesses and hashes, enforce export/import compatibility budgets, and publish the file atomically and durably with its digest and history scope.
Preserve current state and preferences on save failure; distinguish a successful file publication from a later refresh failure and retain old migration history as archive evidence.

rows.purpose: Locate the physical identity required at a named Home destination and inspect its current position.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-TARGET need the wanted-piece lookup in solving-workflow section 4. Preserve the exact Home destination-to-identity mapping without planning a solution.
requirements: Treat the supplied Home destination as the wanted immutable identity and resolve where that identity is now; keep the current occupant and wanted piece distinct.
Return exact current piece data at a known revision, without choosing a target, producing a solving macro or using colour equality as identity.

rows.purpose: Save an explicitly chosen portable interchange log of recorded work.
rows.reason: F-SESSION retains file saving as the counterpart of log export; charter section 4 replaces the live MPUlt bridge and centralizes file commands. Merge delivery with the same log contract used by U1-038.
requirements: Use an explicit supported format and durable atomic publication with digest, model and state identity; failure must leave session state and any previous destination recoverable.

Any MPUlt v1 encoding must use verified offline numbering and declared full-model limits without loading the retained runtime; preserve an exact witnessed 1.0 archive when interchange data is less expressive.
rows.notes: Supported interchange formats are decided at the format freeze; retaining the save purpose does not select the 0.4 wire format or runtime.

rows.purpose: Choose unfinished work in the active orbit with residual and block context and explained candidates.
rows.reason: F-TARGET retains unfinished-position navigation, while solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4.2 give locked Next and block context priority. Replace flat positional wrapping with explicit residual-aware candidate navigation.
requirements: Keep position errors, orientation errors and A/B buffer residuals distinct; respect locked Next and current block/protection context and explain candidates without choosing a solving macro.
Wait for the solver choice; exhausted ordinary candidates with residual work must expose the endgame rather than claim completion or unlock protection.
Only an exact full-orbit completion check may report completion, with a gap or unknown reference reported explicitly.

rows.purpose: Inspect and recover work from a bounded verified C600 proof-log file without losing the current session.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-MIGRATE retain proof import; AGENTS.md requires complete validation before writes and a recovery checkpoint. Owner migration path B and the command table require one-way legacy handling and explicit confirmed file scope.
requirements: B-004: Atomically admit import/replay work alongside other long jobs; prove single-session admission with an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture.

Bound compressed/expanded size, transaction and primitive counts; reject duplicate fields, non-finite values and invalid encodings, verify every legal witness and hash before one recovery transaction, and preserve current preferences.
Bind confirmation to identical file bytes and current model/state/workspace/protection revisions; cancellation or failure must retain prior progress, and durable success must survive refresh failure.
Archive 0.4 history and start 1.0 history at the imported migration state; proof-file import supplements the owner-selected locked-database migration and must not modify a legacy source.

rows.purpose: Analyse named buffers and a solver-named target to compare legal guarded setup frames and their evidence.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-CHECK retain buffer/setup analysis under solving-workflow sections 3.1 and 7, where named-target setup search is allowed. Re-host it with explicit roles and explained candidates instead of automatic target selection and fixed hidden assumptions.
requirements: Require the target named by the solver and explicit buffer positions, distinguishing their changing occupants; show setup paths, frame coverage, finite witnesses, cost precision and reference/collateral evidence.
Proposed setups must use caps touching neither buffer and remain editable drafts; the solver chooses the macro and executes explicitly.
Full-operation preview must certify actual protection against every scope and all labels; missing relocation or frame evidence must be a gap, never an invented solution or automatic unlock.

rows.purpose: Recover the saved state and recorded provenance of a full-model legacy log with its saved history pointer verified.
rows.reason: F-MIGRATE and F-SESSION retain legacy work recovery; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-migration establishes a one-way import boundary and charter section 4 excludes the inherited runtime. Replace live-bridge import with bounded offline compatibility.
requirements: B-004: Admit legacy log replay atomically with other long jobs and prove single-session admission with an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture.

Validate the full-model header, description, checksum, colours, bounded move tokens, saved pointer and redo tail against verified offline numbering and full labelled legal replay; reject unsupported profiles before writes.
Preserve current preferences and timer with a recovery checkpoint and exact file/revision-bound confirmation; never load the old application or modify a source file.
Preserve legacy active history and redo evidence in the migration archive, with 1.0 undo/history beginning at the imported state rather than continuing across the 0.4 boundary.

rows.purpose: Install a completely validated session record as recoverable imported work with exact state and provenance.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-MIGRATE retain verified replay/import under AGENTS.md transactional persistence rules. Charter section 4 and the owner migration decision of 2 October place publication and history boundaries in the new session store.
requirements: B-004: Admit record validation and import atomically with other long jobs; verify concurrent admission using an instrumented fixture.

Verify model/root identity, every legal recipe and witness count, chronological pre/post/final hashes and all size budgets before any persistent change; preserve current preferences and the prior recovery checkpoint.

Require confirmation bound to the same record digest and current revisions, publish once transactionally and invalidate old preview authority; cancellation, write failure and refresh failure must preserve the correct durable outcome.
For 0.4 input, retain historical evidence in the one-way migration archive and root 1.0 history at its imported checkpoint; the original session directory remains unchanged.

rows.purpose: Establish that the active renderer geometry, identifiers and legal turn semantics correspond exactly to the full model.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM supports trustworthy F-FIND and F-EXECUTE under charter section 2. Charter section 4 replaces the retained MPUlt host, so redesign verification for the new canonical renderer and oracle boundary.
requirements: B-004: Admit correspondence verification atomically with other long jobs; prove single-session admission with an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture.

Tie verified correspondence to immutable model and build identities, covering all 259,800 sticker slots and 1,200 legal generators with exact IDs and finite legal witness semantics before enabling guarded interaction.
Keep legacy mapping only as offline compatibility/oracle data; source or synthetic correspondence verification cannot assert actual Windows/DirectX, picking or performance equivalence.

rows.purpose: Save a reusable work set with explicit live-query, frozen-identity or frozen-position membership semantics.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-REUSE need persistent work sets; solving-workflow section 4.3 distinguishes three membership kinds. Extend the existing frozen-set purpose into that explicit contract through the session store.
requirements: Retain the set kind: a live query re-evaluates, frozen identities follow their pieces and frozen positions retain destinations with changing occupants; validate names, members and resource limits before publication.

Capture frozen membership at an exact reviewed revision and keep named-set replacement explicit; stored sets must not narrow the full mechanical model or confer interaction/turn permission by themselves.

rows.purpose: Compose explicitly supplied macros by concatenation, inversion, commutator or conjugation and inspect their complete effect.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-MACRO retain solver-directed macro editing under solving-workflow section 7. These rows share one algebraic composition purpose, and charter section 2 preserves chronological source-to-destination mathematics.
requirements: A-03: Normalize validated star steps before inversion or composition so an omitted sign has its accepted +1 meaning; inverse, conjugate and commutator must agree with explicit-sign legal replay.
B-004: Admit composition/preview work atomically with other long jobs and verify the single-session limit with an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture.
Preserve A then B chronological concatenation, A B A^-1 B^-1 commutators and A B A^-1 conjugates, with complete finite witnesses and collateral; do not choose operands or solving macros from state.
Composition produces a draft and fresh full-effect review, never an automatic execution or reused permission.

rows.purpose: Save the solver's reviewed finite operation as a reusable versioned personal macro.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE retain the personal macro library; solving-workflow section 4.1 requires every reuse to receive a fresh review. Move persistence out of broad preferences into explicit macro records and provenance.
requirements: Store immutable normalized steps, finite legal witnesses, model identity, macro revision, complete support/effect and solver provenance; saved analysis must not carry execution authority.
Make replacement/version choice explicit and validate names and data before publication; a changed role, target, macro revision or protection requires new complete-operation analysis.
Saving must not commit puzzle moves or invent an applicable solving macro.

rows.purpose: Prepare a reproducible legal scramble and apply it only through the solver's explicit practice or session action.
rows.reason: F-LEARN retains scrambling under the practice-copy decision in owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 7. Charter section 4 and the command table unify preview and commit, replacing the separate immediate-apply path.
requirements: B-004: Admit scramble preparation atomically with other long jobs and prove single-session admission with an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture.
Record the seed, length, full legal word, model identity and scramble provenance; generate from explicit deterministic inputs without clock-based decisions inside the mathematical engine.

Use a clearly labelled isolated full-model practice copy for onboarding; outside it preserve the current session and all protection, and execute only through the ordinary fresh-review command path after explicit action.
Failed preparation must retain the previous draft/provenance when state is unchanged; a durable applied scramble must retain its receipt even if refresh fails.

rows.purpose: Apply solver-entered legal turns to the chosen draft or live state with exact protection and journal semantics.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE retain manual turns; solving-workflow section 4.1 separates draft input from live operations and section 4.3 requires stable Grip/Twist meanings. Replace native token dispatch with the canonical command path.
requirements: X-02: Turn receipts and paired refreshes must avoid checkpoint-blob scans and unbounded status rebuilding; measure cost as checkpoint history grows.
Resolve exact legal generators from explicit stable Grip/Twist input and fresh pre-state/view/protection revisions; preserve chronological batch witnesses and access to all 1,200 generators.
Draft input changes only the selected phase and forecast; each live turn is a complete protected operation and cannot borrow future cleanup, with no commit key repeat or silent key retargeting.
Journal a live operation once transactionally and report its durable receipt separately from renderer refresh or scratch feedback.

rows.purpose: Review the solver's complete finite operation effect, witness, frames, collateral and protection without applying it.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-COMPOSE require complete Prepare/Macro/Cleanup analysis under solving-workflow section 4.1. Charter sections 2 and 5 preserve mathematics and require exact visible evidence across the new layers.
requirements: A-01: Deep-freeze normalized recipe steps, move lists, expanded witnesses and certificate inputs at preview; later caller mutation must not change the pending operation or its eventual replay.
B-004: Admit preview work atomically with other long jobs and prove single-session admission with an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture.

Analyse all 259,800 labels and full collateral in chronological source-to-destination order; bind role, target, frame, macro, state, workspace and protection revisions and support Net or Strict checks at the requested boundaries.

Distinguish legal execution permission, goal attainment, evidence status and exact completion; explicitly supplied words or symbolic stars may be expanded and analysed, while the program must not select a solving macro.
A preview mutates only draft/review state, remains resource-bounded and cancellable, and exposes unchecked prefixes or missing certificates as such.

rows.purpose: Receive position and orientation insertion macros chosen from the current orbit state.
rows.reason: Solving-workflow section 7 and charter section 5 prohibit the program choosing or outputting a solving macro. The insertion planner chooses stars, orientation transfers and endgame corrections even when its first target is named, so this purpose crosses the boundary.
rows.notes: Proposal requiring owner signature; Session.suggest (session.py:212) invokes the state-driven Planner.next (core.py:294), including automatically chosen later batch targets. Target candidates, named-target setup analysis and exact residual inspection survive as separate purposes.

rows.purpose: Execute exactly the complete operation explicitly approved by the solver once and preserve its durable outcome.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE retains preview-bound commit; solving-workflow sections 2 and 4.1 require current full-state and protection checks over the whole operation. Charter section 4 places a single gated command above one transactional session publication.
requirements: A-01: Journal and execute the identical immutable normalized witness, effect and certificate captured at preview; caller mutation must never produce a replay mismatch.
X-02: Commit receipts must use lightweight checkpoint metadata and avoid checkpoint-blob scans or history-wide status reconstruction; measure cost as checkpoints accumulate.

Require explicit solver action and recheck token, head, full-state hash, all relevant revisions, macro/role/frame bindings and orbit/position/identity/block protection before chronological complete-operation execution.

Publish labels, journal, related workspace/protection changes and recovery bookkeeping in one transaction; retain branches and required automatic checkpoints, with command identity ensuring at-most-once retry.
Return a durable receipt even when display refresh fails, invalidate spent authority and never unlock protection or select a different macro to make execution possible.

rows.purpose: Discard a pending operation preview and its execution token without changing the committed puzzle.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-EXECUTE require the solver to back out before execution under solving-workflow section 4. Preserve cancellation of preview authority separately from cancelling a running analysis.
requirements: Invalidate the pending certificate/token while retaining committed labels, journal history, current protection and the solver's editable draft; cancellation must not execute or undo an operation.

rows.purpose: Receive a revision-bound display refresh alongside a completed command while retaining its authoritative outcome.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and F-SESSION retain paired state/command feedback; the command table separates durable commit outcome from refresh and owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 6 requires linked revisions. Replace native piggyback replies with coherent command receipts and view updates.
requirements: X-02: Paired command refreshes must avoid checkpoint-blob scans and unbounded status reconstruction; verify response work over growing checkpoint populations.
Build any paired full/delta update from the exact completed command revision using immutable bases; never combine another state revision with the command receipt.
Once committed, retain success and its command identity even if snapshot construction, transport or rendering fails; report applied/display-stale and refresh without re-executing.

rows.purpose: Explore a known reproducible legal scramble in a clearly labelled full-model practice session.
rows.reason: F-LEARN retains a recorded example; owner-decisions-2026-10-02-design section 7 supplies a practice copy instead of making the solver reset personal progress to use a demo. Re-host the witnessed example in the learning flow.
requirements: B-004: Admit recorded-example preparation atomically with other long jobs and verify single-session admission using an instrumented concurrent-submission fixture.
Bind the recorded finite legal word, seed and length to frozen model identity and verifiable full-state hashes; retain scramble provenance and all collateral.

Use isolated practice data with no personal-session reset, replay the example only after explicit solver action through the normal protected command path, and preserve the previous draft on pre-publication failure.

rows.purpose: Keep command entry bounded, authenticated where needed and unable to bypass model or permission validation.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM protects every flow, and charter section 4 makes the command layer the only mutating entry. Replace 0.4 HTTP-specific guards with the selected local boundary while retaining validation and scoped process authentication.
requirements: Validate command identity, argument types, sizes, nesting, model and context before mutation; reject unknown commands through typed errors and share identical gates across keys, menus and other entry paths.
Where an owned local transport exists, bind authentication and shutdown to its launch and restrict ingress to the intended local peer; do not expose credentials in public diagnostics.
Keep transport/platform checks outside the mathematical engine and do not require a public listener or external service to use the application.

rows.purpose: Run bounded long analyses and recovery operations responsively with consistent admission, cancellation and outcomes.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-SESSION retain job handling; charter section 4 and the command table place it in the command layer above the session store. Replace the racy HTTP queue with a single consistent job lifecycle for the surviving operations.
requirements: B-004: Make active-job reservation, publication and release atomic per session; an instrumented barrier fixture must prove concurrent submissions cannot bypass the one-active-job gate.
Run expensive work outside the UI thread on revision-bound inputs, with bounded resources, cooperative cancellation, typed terminal results and busy availability shared by all entry paths.
Keep cancellation and display failures distinct from durable command receipts; omit the deleted insertion planner and never schedule automatic solving or execution.
